goals.objective:
Objective: Improve the time tracker’s layout, visual hierarchy and UX, and add an automated layout audit so regressions fail verification. Work through the phases in order. After each phase, npm run lint && npm run typecheck && npm test && npm run build and (from Phase 0 on) npm run ui:audit must pass.

Previous Context: We have restyled the app using TailwindCSS and shadcn components. See @.agent/screenshots as a sample of how it looks. Now we need to improve the design.

Hard constraints

Same as before: shadcn/ui components only, tokens only (no hard-coded hex in components), no changes to lib/ signatures or removed or weakened tests, no new dependencies except @axe-core/playwright, no git commits, a note in .agent/PROGRESS.md after each phase.
Use US English in all UI copy (“Color”, “Organize”).
Minimum text size is 12px. Muted text must reach a 4.5:1 contrast ratio in both themes.

Phases and acceptance criteria

Layout audit harness
scripts/ui-audit.ts (run by npm run ui:audit) visits every route at 375, 768 and 1280px, in light and dark, and in three states: seeded, empty, and running-timer. It uses a documented seed fixture.
It fails with a nonzero exit if any of these is true: the page scrolls horizontally; any element overflows its nearest card; any text input is narrower than 120px; any button or link on viewports of 768px or less has a hit area under 40×40px; axe reports a violation.
It saves both viewport-height and full-page screenshots to .agent/screenshots/, named <page>-<width>-<theme>-<state>.png.
Initially, the audit is expected to fail on the known bugs below. Record the failures in PROGRESS.md before fixing.
Shell and responsive fixes
At 768px the sidebar becomes an icon rail with tooltips. The full sidebar shows only at 1024px and above.
Sidebar height fills the viewport and stays fixed while content scrolls.
Mobile bottom nav gets bottom padding on the content and a safe-area inset, and never covers the last element.
The top bar shows the page title or breadcrumb on the left and the running-timer indicator and theme toggle on the right.
Categories redesign
The add form is a single row on desktop and wraps cleanly below 640px. The Name input has flex-1 min-w-0 and is at least 200px wide wherever it appears. The color picker opens in a popover instead of showing as inline swatches.
Cards show the color dot, name, hours this week, entry count and a thin share-of-total bar. They have no inline picker.
Card actions live in an overflow menu: Rename, Change color (opens the popover with a confirm step), Delete. Delete keeps the entry-count confirmation dialog.
Swatches in the picker are at least 32px. All cards in a row are equal height.
Dashboard
The timer card is the hero. Idle shows a description input, category select and a large Start button. Running shows a large tabular-nums clock, a pulsing indicator, a Stop button and the elapsed-since-start time.
Stat cards use a 2×2 grid below 768px. A delta appears only when a real comparison exists. Otherwise the dash is removed, not rendered.
The bar chart is stacked by category, includes days with zero entries for the selected range, and has a 7d / 30d / month toggle. X labels read “Thu 22”. Tooltips show per-category durations.
The donut legend is sorted by duration descending, shows “Name · 27%” without wrapping, and shows a clean empty state.
Recent entries has “View all” aligned to the right of the header, and each row shows the time range.
Entries
Filters are one row at 768px and above. Below that, they collapse into a “Filters” button that opens a sheet, with active filters shown as removable chips. “Clear” shows only when a filter is active.
Day headers stick while scrolling. Row hit areas are at least 44px tall on mobile.
Each row’s menu includes Resume (starts a timer with the same description and category), Duplicate, Edit and Delete. Delete keeps the Undo toast.
A currently running timer appears as a live row at the top of Today.
Tests cover Resume, Duplicate, and the filter-chip logic.
Settings
Content is capped at about 720px wide and centered on desktop.
Export and Import are merged into one “Data” card with a data summary (entry and category counts, approximate size).
Import uses a styled drop zone with drag-and-drop and a keyboard-accessible button. The paste-JSON option sits in a collapsed accordion.
Remove the native file input styling. Validation errors show inline.
Typography and contrast
All muted text meets 4.5:1 in both themes, and no text is under 12px.
Spacing uses a consistent scale, and headings use a defined type scale from tokens.
Zero axe violations across all pages, widths and themes in ui:audit.
UX details
document.title shows the running timer (e.g. “● 00:42:10 · Time Tracker”) while a timer is active and resets when it stops.
Keyboard shortcuts: N opens Add entry, and Space starts or stops the timer when focus isn’t in an input. A ? dialog lists them.
First-run state: with no data, the dashboard shows a welcome card with a “Create your first category” step and a “Load sample data” button.
Tests cover the title behavior, the shortcut guards (no firing while typing), and the first-run state.
Final audit
ui:audit passes with no failures on all routes, widths, themes and states.
Produce a .agent/screenshots/INDEX.md listing every screenshot, so review is quick.

Done when: all phases are complete, the full verify command and ui:audit both pass from a clean checkout, and no lib/ signatures or tests changed.

**Objective:** Add Supabase auth and database persistence to the time tracker without changing the UI or the pure logic in `lib/`. The app must keep working with no Supabase config by falling back to the localStorage backend. Work through the phases in order. After each phase, `npm run lint && npm run typecheck && npm test && npm run build && npm run ui:audit` must pass.

**Hard constraints**
- Do not edit `.env.local`, read any real credentials, or run any command that contacts a remote database or Supabase project (no `supabase db push`, no network calls in tests). Never use or reference a `service_role` or `sb_secret_` key anywhere.
- Allowed new dependencies: `@supabase/supabase-js`, `@supabase/ssr`, `@tanstack/react-query` (already installed). No others.
- Keep `lib/storage.ts` and its tests unchanged. Keep exported signatures and behavior of the pure functions in `lib/` (aggregation, filtering, validation, duration helpers). No removed or weakened tests.
- Use the publishable key env var `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY`. On the server, use `getClaims()`, never `getSession()`.
- If `package.json` has Next.js 16 or later, the session-refresh file is `proxy.ts`. If earlier, it is `middleware.ts`. Check the version and state which in PROGRESS.md.
- No git commits or pushes. Append a note to `.agent/PROGRESS.md` after each phase.

**Phases and acceptance criteria**

0. **Repository abstraction (no behavior change)**
   - `lib/data/types.ts` defines an async `DataRepository` covering categories (list, create, update, delete), entries (list, create, update, delete, restore-with-same-id for Undo), the running timer (get, start, stop), and `exportAll`/`importAll`.
   - `lib/data/local-repository.ts` implements it on top of the existing `lib/storage.ts`.
   - A shared contract test suite runs against both the local repository and an in-memory fake. It covers CRUD, delete-category-reassigns-entries, timer start/stop creating an entry, and import validation.
   - A `DataProvider` and hooks expose the repository to the UI through TanStack Query. All pages read and write through the hooks, not `lib/storage.ts` directly. Loading skeletons and error states exist for every query.
   - All existing tests and `ui:audit` still pass unchanged.

1. **Schema and RLS (SQL only)**
   - `supabase/migrations/0001_init.sql` creates `categories` (id uuid, user_id default `auth.uid()`, name, color, created_at), `entries` (id, user_id, description, category_id nullable referencing categories on delete set null, started_at, ended_at, check ended_at > started_at), and `running_timers` (user_id unique, description, category_id, started_at).
   - Indexes on `(user_id, started_at)` for entries and `user_id` for the others.
   - RLS enabled on every table, with separate select/insert/update/delete policies for the `authenticated` role, using `(select auth.uid()) = user_id`. Insert and update policies include `with check` so a user cannot write rows for another user.
   - A `stop_timer(p_end timestamptz)` function (security invoker) that inserts the entry and deletes the timer atomically.
   - `scripts/check-rls.ts` (run by `npm run check:rls`) parses the migration and fails if any table lacks RLS or any of the four policies. `supabase/README.md` explains how a human applies the migration.

2. **Supabase clients, env and session refresh**
   - `lib/supabase/client.ts` (browser), `lib/supabase/server.ts`, and the `updateSession` helper, following the current `@supabase/ssr` pattern. The root `proxy.ts` (or `middleware.ts`) is thin and only refreshes the session and redirects unauthenticated users to `/login` when the Supabase backend is active.
   - `lib/config.ts` decides the backend: Supabase if both env vars are set, otherwise local. A unit test covers both cases.
   - `.env.example` documents the two variables (no real values). Tests for the helpers use mocked cookies and clients.

3. **Auth UI**
   - `/login` and `/signup` (email and password), `/auth/callback` (code exchange) and `/auth/confirm` (email OTP), and sign out. Forms use shadcn components, show inline errors, and are fully keyboard-accessible.
   - An account menu shows the user's email and a Sign out action. It is shown only when the Supabase backend is active.
   - When the backend is local, none of the auth routes or the account menu appear.
   - `ui:audit` covers `/login` and `/signup` at all three widths, in both themes, with zero axe violations.

4. **SupabaseRepository**
   - `lib/data/supabase-repository.ts` implements `DataRepository`: maps snake_case to camelCase, maps `null` category to the app's Uncategorized category, and converts Supabase errors into typed errors the UI can toast.
   - The shared contract suite also runs against it using a small fake Supabase client. An optional integration run executes only when `SUPABASE_TEST_URL` and `SUPABASE_TEST_KEY` are set, and is skipped otherwise.
   - A backend factory returns the right repository based on `lib/config.ts`.

5. **Data behavior**
   - Mutations are optimistic with rollback and an error toast. Undo-after-delete restores the row with the same id.
   - The timer lives in `running_timers`. Stop uses the `stop_timer` function. The tab title and top-bar indicator keep working.
   - Data refetches on window focus, so a timer started on another device appears.
   - Tests cover rollback on failure, undo, and timer start/stop through the fake.

6. **Local-to-cloud migration and settings**
   - After the first sign-in, if localStorage holds data and the cloud account is empty, show a dialog offering to import N entries and M categories. Import is idempotent (re-running does not duplicate). Non-UUID local ids are mapped to new UUIDs consistently. On success, offer to clear local data.
   - The Settings page gets an Account card (email, Sign out). Export and Import use the active repository. "Reset all data" deletes only the signed-in user's rows, behind the existing confirmation.
   - Theme and time format remain local preferences.
   - Tests cover idempotent import, id mapping, and reset scope.

7. **Hardening**
   - `ui:audit` passes for all routes, widths and themes in the local backend, including loading and error states.
   - A script fails the build if `service_role`, `sb_secret_` or `SUPABASE_SERVICE` appears anywhere in the repository.
   - README gets a "Supabase setup" section (project, auth URLs, applying the migration, env vars).

**Done when:** all phases pass the full verify command plus `check:rls`, the app still works fully with no Supabase env set, and `git diff` shows `lib/storage.ts` and its tests unchanged.
